sections.h2: Where is Council Bluffs, Iowa, and what is the Loess Hills setting?
sections.html:
Council Bluffs is the seat of Pottawattamie County, on the east bank of the Missouri River directly across from Omaha, Nebraska. A small part of the city reaches into Mills County.

The city lies in the Loess Hills, so the ground rolls and drops in a way most of Iowa does not. It covers about 46 square miles at 978 feet, and Lake Manawa State Park sits at the southern edge. Viewpoints include Fairmont Park, Kirn Park, the Lincoln Monument and the Lewis and Clark Monument. The 2020 census counted 62,799 people, and the 2024 estimate is 62,665.

sections.h2: How did Council Bluffs get its name and start?
sections.html:
Lewis and Clark named the bluff after a meeting with the Otoe on August 2, 1804. The town itself was called Kanesville until about 1852 or 1853, and it was incorporated as Council Bluffs on January 19, 1853.

  • 1840s: Fort Croghan was built in 1842 and destroyed by a flood the same year. Latter-day Saints arrived in large numbers from 1846, and Kanesville became the main outfitting point and head of the Mormon Trail.
  • 1860s: Lincoln designated Council Bluffs the starting point of the transcontinental railroad, completed in 1869. The Chicago and North Western arrived in 1867.
  • 1870s and later: the Union Pacific Missouri River Bridge opened in 1872. By the 1930s the city was the fifth largest rail center in the country.

Mile 0 of the line is marked by a gold spike monument at 21st Street and 9th Avenue.

sections.h2: What drives the Council Bluffs economy?
sections.html:
Data centers, casinos, rail and food processing all matter here. Google finished the first phase of its Council Bluffs data centers in 2009, and a third phase announced in March 2014 brought its investment to $1.5 billion. Google reported more than 300 jobs on site as of June 2016.

The casino sector began with Bluffs Run Greyhound Park in 1986 and riverboat casinos in the mid-1990s. Ameristar, Harrah's and Horseshoe operate here, and gambling revenue reached nearly $434 million by 2005, making it the 19th largest casino market in the country.

Other employers include Tyson Foods and ConAgra plants, and a coal-fired MidAmerican Energy plant built in 2007 as a billion-dollar investment. Griffin Pipe closed its plant, with about 250 employees, in March 2014. Layoffs like that one are part of why some owners sell quickly.

sections.h2: Which school districts and colleges serve Council Bluffs?
sections.html:
The Council Bluffs Community School District serves most of the city, with 10 elementary schools, two middle schools and two high schools, Abraham Lincoln and Thomas Jefferson. The Lewis Central Community School District serves the southern part of the city.

Other institutions include the Iowa School for the Deaf, which has been here since 1870, Iowa Western Community College and a Buena Vista University location. Because two districts divide the city, confirm the district for your address before describing the house to a buyer.

sections.h2: What roads, rail and airports serve Council Bluffs?
sections.html:
Interstate 80 and Interstate 29 meet at Council Bluffs, and U.S. 6 and 275 and Iowa 92 and 192 also serve the city. The Loess Hills National Scenic Byway passes through. The Interstate 480 bridge connects to downtown Omaha.

  • Rail: Union Pacific, BNSF, Iowa Interstate and Canadian National.
  • Commercial flights: mostly through Omaha's Eppley Airfield.
  • General aviation: Council Bluffs Municipal Airport.

The Omaha link means a Council Bluffs house is often compared with Omaha-area alternatives, so a seller should think about commuters on both sides of the river.

sections.h2: Which Council Bluffs neighborhoods and areas should sellers know?
sections.html:
Named areas include Downtown, Old Town, West End, Casino Row, Twin City, Manawa, South End, Oakland-Fairview, Madison Avenue and Huntington Avenue.

The western part of the city has an unusual history. Carter Lake seceded in 1926 after a river course change cut it off, and a flood in 1881 cut off a Missouri River channel and formed Lake Manawa. Anyone selling near the river should keep that in mind, since the river has moved the boundaries here before.

In 2010, the Iowa DNR found that air in the central city exceeded the national lead standard, and in 2011 the EPA cited Clean Water Act violations at the Griffin Pipe plant. Neither fact is a reason to avoid selling, but buyers may research the neighborhood, and sellers can expect questions.

sections.h2: When does Pottawattamie County property tax become delinquent?
sections.html:
Property tax in Iowa is billed in two installments that turn delinquent on October 1 and April 1. Iowa Code 445.37 adds timing rules that apply to Council Bluffs owners.

  • If September 30 or March 31 falls on a weekend, delinquency moves to the second business day of the next month.
  • To avoid interest on mailed payments, the treasurer must receive the check by the last business day of the month before the delinquent date, or it must be postmarked before that date.
  • Online payments through a county treasurer's authorized site follow their own cutoff at midnight.

If you sell mid-year, the title company usually prorates the bill. Confirm what has been paid with the Pottawattamie County Treasurer first.

sections.h2: What does Iowa require when a Council Bluffs house is sold?
sections.html:
Iowa asks sellers to report the condition of the land, not only the building. Under Iowa Code 558.69, a groundwater hazard statement goes to the recorder with the declaration of value.

If none of the listed conditions exist, no separate statement is filed. The first page of the deed carries a prescribed line saying so instead. A recorder must refuse a deed that is missing the required statement. The transfer tax under Iowa Code 428A.1 is 80 cents per $500 and does not apply when no consideration is paid.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Council Bluffs house work?
sections.html:
You tell the buyer about the house, receive a written cash offer, and choose a closing date. There are no showings and no waiting on a buyer's mortgage.

A title company or attorney handles the deed and recorder filings in Pottawattamie County. Compare the offer with the cost of repairs and the months a listing could take, and say no if it does not fit.

faqs.q: Is Council Bluffs the county seat of Pottawattamie County?
faqs.a: Yes. Council Bluffs is the seat of Pottawattamie County, and a small part of the city extends into Mills County.

faqs.q: How many people live in Council Bluffs?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 62,799 residents, and the Census Bureau estimates 62,680 as of July 1, 2025.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Council Bluffs house in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in the Council Bluffs Community School District. The southern part is in the Lewis Central Community School District.

faqs.q: When did Council Bluffs get its name?
faqs.a: It was called Kanesville until about 1852 or 1853 and was incorporated as Council Bluffs on January 19, 1853. The name comes from a 1804 meeting between Lewis and Clark and the Otoe.

faqs.q: When are Iowa property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: The first installment is delinquent from October 1 and the second from April 1. A weekend deadline moves to the second business day of the following month.
